vulnerabilities.title: Missing Owner Filter in getScheduledDosesInRange
vulnerabilities.description: getScheduledDosesInRange(startDate, endDate) queries all scheduled doses in a date range without filtering by owner. In a two-user app (Victor/Nadia), User A can retrieve User B's scheduled doses by calling this function directly.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Scheduled doses returned without owner filter
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: User Victor calls getScheduledDosesInRange('2026-07-01', '2026-07-31'). Returns all 200 doses in range including 120 from Nadia. Victor accesses Nadia's full injection schedule.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add owner parameter and filter at database level before returning results

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Owner Filter in getDoseLogsInRange
vulnerabilities.description: getDoseLogsInRange(startDate, endDate) retrieves all dose logs in a date range without owner filtering. User A can query and retrieve all dose logs (including symptoms, injection sites, notes) from User B.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Dose logs returned without owner filter
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: User Nadia calls getDoseLogsInRange('2026-06-01', '2026-07-31'). Receives 85 dose logs including Victor's symptom severity scores and personal notes.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Filter by owner at query time in database operations layer

vulnerabilities.title: Client-Side Only Data Filtering After Unrestricted Query
vulnerabilities.description: Calendar calls getScheduledDosesInRange() and getDoseLogsInRange() without owner filters, receiving ALL data. Filtering via filterByOwner() is applied client-side AFTER data is already in React state, exposing unfiltered data to browser dev tools.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Filtering applied to state after unrestricted retrieval
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Attacker opens React DevTools, inspects state.monthDoses directly. Sees 200 dose objects before filtering. localStorage can also be inspected to manipulate viewFilter.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Query only current user's data at database layer, not in component filters

vulnerabilities.title: No Validation That saveScheduledDoses Owner Matches Current User
vulnerabilities.description: saveScheduledDoses(doses, owner) accepts an arbitrary owner parameter with no validation. A compromised client can pass owner='Nadia' even when logged in as Victor.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Operations accept owner parameter without auth validation
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor is logged in. Malicious JavaScript calls saveScheduledDoses(doses, 'Nadia'). Doses are saved under Nadia's account instead of Victor's.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Store current user in protected context, validate in every operation against authenticated user from Supabase session

vulnerabilities.title: localStorage Not Cleared on User Switch
vulnerabilities.description: getLastOwner()/setLastOwner() use localStorage for persistence. On shared devices, localStorage persists across sessions. When User B opens browser after User A, LAST_OWNER_KEY still shows User A.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: User context persists in localStorage across device sessions
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor uses app on shared iPad, closes Safari. Nadia opens Safari. Any dose Nadia logs has owner='Victor' due to stale localStorage value.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove user identity from localStorage. Derive it from Supabase auth.getSession() only. Clear all user state on logout.

vulnerabilities.title: Single Shared Supabase Account for Multiple Local Users
vulnerabilities.description: App runs on one shared Supabase account provisioned out-of-band. Data isolation between Victor and Nadia relies entirely on RLS policies (not shown). No per-user authentication. If RLS is misconfigured, all user data is exposed.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Data isolation depends on RLS alone; no per-user auth
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: RLS policy is buggy (missing WHERE owner filter). One sync call returns ALL data from both users. Or: VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY leaks, attacker calls Supabase API directly.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Verify all RLS policies are correctly deployed. Test RLS policies with cross-user queries in test suite.

vulnerabilities.title: Timestamp Trust in Last-Write-Wins (LWW) Sync
vulnerabilities.description: Cloud sync uses Last-Write-Wins based on client-provided updatedAt timestamps. A client can set arbitrary timestamps, causing newer remote edits to be overwritten by local rows with fake future timestamps.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: LWW conflict resolution trusts client-supplied timestamps
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor's local row has updatedAt='2099-01-01'. Nadia's remote edit has updatedAt='2026-07-27'. Sync chooses Victor's row (newer timestamp), overwriting Nadia's valid edit.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use server-assigned timestamps from Supabase (database-generated updated_at), not client-provided fields

vulnerabilities.title: getAllDoseLogs() Called Without Owner Filter
vulnerabilities.description: HalfLife.tsx calls getAllDoseLogs() which returns ALL dose logs from all users. Active Levels chart displays both users' dosing history without separation.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: All dose logs retrieved and charted without filtering
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor opens Active Levels page. Chart displays both his and Nadia's peptide series. Victor infers Nadia's compound use, timing, and dosing patterns.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Modify getAllDoseLogs() to filter by owner. Chart only current user's data.

vulnerabilities.title: getProtocols() Returns All Protocols Without Owner Check
vulnerabilities.description: getProtocols(status) retrieves all protocols matching status without filtering by owner. A user can see all protocols (active/paused/completed) created by the other user.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Protocol queries not filtered by owner
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: User calls getProtocols('active'). Receives all active protocols from both Victor and Nadia, including private protocol metadata.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add owner filter to getProtocols query at database layer

vulnerabilities.title: View Filter Can Be Manually Manipulated
vulnerabilities.description: ViewFilterContext stores filter state ('all'/'Victor'/'Nadia'). User could manually set filter to another user via browser dev tools, then query database for that user's data. Filter is client-side state with no auth binding.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: View filter not bound to authenticated user identity
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Victor uses dev tools to set ViewFilterContext filter='Nadia', then manually calls getScheduledDosesInRange(). Could retrieve Nadia's data.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Enforce owner filter at database layer only. Never allow view filter to differ from authenticated user.

summary: pepdose is a multi-user medication tracking PWA with CRITICAL multi-user data isolation vulnerabilities. Database queries return unfiltered data across users. Client-side filtering after retrieval provides no protection. Owner validation is missing from operations. localStorage persists user context across sessions. A shared Supabase account with no per-user auth means RLS is the sole defense. Either user can trivially access the other's full dose history, protocols, symptoms, and injection data.
recommendations: URGENT: Add owner parameter and filter to all database queries (getScheduledDosesInRange, getDoseLogsInRange, getProtocols, getAllDoseLogs, getVials, getHealthMarkers). Filter at query time, not in components.
URGENT: Add mandatory owner validation in every database write. Verify owner parameter matches authenticated user from Supabase auth.getSession().
URGENT: Remove user identity from localStorage. Derive current user from Supabase auth session only. Clear all local state on logout.
HIGH: Verify and test all RLS policies in supabase/migrations/. Ensure every query filters by auth.uid(). Test with cross-user queries.
HIGH: Replace client-supplied timestamps with server timestamps. Sync should trust remote updated_at from Supabase only.
HIGH: Make ViewFilterContext read-only, derived from authenticated user. User can only view their own data.
MEDIUM: Add integration tests verifying query results are filtered by owner. Test: user A queries, confirm no user B data.
MEDIUM: Implement per-user IndexedDB namespacing to prevent cross-user leakage in browser storage.
LOW: Document RLS design in CLAUDE.md. Include threat model for shared device/browser scenarios.
scope: XSS vectors: PASS (no unsafe innerHTML or eval)
